response.explanation:
The handler filters `guests` into `uniqueGuests`. That filter removes emails that are already attendees and emails on the blacklist. Only `uniqueGuests` is saved as new attendees. The email step then calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the unfiltered input. A concrete input: the booking already has attendee a@x.com, and the request is `guests: [a@x.com, b@x.com]`. Only b@x.com is added, but a@x.com is also sent a "guests added" email. A blacklisted address in `guests` also gets an email even though it was deliberately skipped. The send is wrapped in a try/catch that only logs, so nothing flags the mismatch.

A second defect is in the permission check. `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)` uses `&&` where `||` is intended. Only a user who passes both checks counts as a team admin or owner. If `isTeamAdmin` includes owners, as I expect, team admins who are not owners are denied. I did not open `isTeamAdmin` or `isTeamOwner` to confirm that. The check also falls back to team id 0 when the event type has no team.
